QF.id: XVI Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_23

question.text: Lean period margin for agricultural commodities is levied because:

answer.text: During the pre-harvest lean period there is uncertainty about the harvest or production volume, which makes spot prices volatile and warrants an additional margin on agricultural commodity contracts
All commodities trade at lower volumes year-round
SEBI mandates additional margin every quarter
Warehouses charge higher storage fees during monsoon

explanation.text: The Logic: The lean period is the pre-harvest window in which the size of the upcoming harvest or production volume is uncertain. This uncertainty translates into elevated volatility in spot prices, which in turn justifies an additional lean period margin on agricultural commodity contracts. The Trap: The lean period concept applies to agricultural commodities, not to all commodities and not on a fixed quarterly cycle. Warehouse charges or monsoon storage costs are not the stated rationale. Note: Specific lean period windows and margin rates are defined per commodity in exchange circulars and move with the relevant crop cycle.
